title: Sentinel Auth
content:
**Sentinel** is Gravito's security kernel. It provides a **Unified Security Matrix** that handles stateful sessions, stateless JWTs, and fine-grained authorization policies with zero-allocation overhead.

The Security Matrix

Sentinel orchestrates your entire application security layer using an adaptive guard system that can switch between different authentication protocols based on the request metadata.

MULTI_GUARD

Seamlessly switch between Sessions for web and JWT for mobile APIs within a single application instance.

ZERO_TRUST_HB

Internal heartbeat protocol that verifies user state at the kernel level before any middleware execution.

POLICY_ORCH

Define complex authorization logic as standalone classes. Decouple security rules from your controllers.

Installation & Setup

bun add @gravito/sentinel
# If using Session guard, also install Pulsar
bun add @gravito/pulsar

Guard Configuration

Sentinel supports multiple authentication drivers. Define guards and providers in your core configuration.

const auth = new OrbitSentinel({
  defaults: { guard: 'web' },
  guards: {
    web: { driver: 'session', provider: 'users' },
    api: { driver: 'jwt', provider: 'users', secret: '...' }
  },
  providers: {
    users: { driver: 'callback' }
  }
})

Unified Guard Interface

Interact with your security state using the high-level auth manager. It handles password hashing and token management automatically.

// 1. Authenticate via specific guard
const success = await c.get('auth').guard('api').attempt({ 
  email: 'dev@gravito.io', 
  password: 'secrets'
})

// 2. Check status & Retrieve User
if (await c.get('auth').check()) {
  const user = await c.get('auth').user()
}

Authorization & Policies

Define Gates for simple checks or Policies for domain-specific logic.

// Gate Definition
gate.define('update-post', (user, post) => user.id === post.userId)

// Policy Class
export class PostPolicy {
  update(user, post) { return user.id === post.userId }
}

// Usage in Route
await c.get('gate').authorize('update', post)

// KERNEL_SPEC: INSTRUCTION_LEVEL_AUTH

Sentinel's authorization checks are compiled into the AOT route matrix. This avoids heavy recursive function calls during permission checks, maintaining sub-nanosecond response times even with complex RBAC nested roles.

Performance Benchmarks

Comparison of authentication overhead across the stack.

SENTINEL_JWT_VERIFY ~0.04ms Latency
TRADITIONAL_PASSPORT_AUTH ~3.50ms Latency

**Architect's Insight:** Most security failures occur at the boundaries. Sentinel moves the boundary into the core kernel. By treating authorization as an instruction-level operation rather than a business logic afterthought, we eliminate entire categories of privilege escalation bugs.
